purchasedGood.description: The catalog.item or catalog.product purchased -- Bazaar sells both under one receipt shape, hence the generic name.

listing.description: Listing purchased. cid is pinned at checkout as the immutable price anchor.

licenseGrant.description: License terms in effect at time of purchase. cid resolved from the listing's own licenseGrant.cid. Required: every listing must carry license terms before it can be sold, so every receipt has one. cid is folded into storefrontSig (see storefrontSig's description) -- this is what freezes the license terms atomically with the purchase itself; there is no separate consent record.

grantedItems.description: The catalog.item refs (uri + cid) this purchase entitles the buyer to download, frozen at purchase time. Single-item purchase: the one item ref. Product purchase: the product's member item refs at time of sale — later edits to product.items do NOT change this grant (a removed item stays downloadable for this buyer; an added item is not). Sorted by uri UTF-8 byte order and de-duplicated by uri. Covered by storefrontSig — see storefrontSig's description for the digest algorithm. Freezes which items, not which bytes: re-uploading an item's master still serves the current file for that URI. Required: a receipt without it cannot reconstruct the signed payload and will not verify. Immutable.

storefrontDid.description: DID of the storefront (Bazaar service instance) that issued this receipt. Verifiers resolve this to get the public key for storefrontSig verification.

merchantDid.description: DID of the merchant this receipt was issued under — the ATProto identity hosting the catalog/storefront (actor.merchant).

storefrontSig.description: Base64url signature by the storefront service keypair (storefrontDid) over a colon-delimited payload of exactly seven fields, in this fixed order: purchasedAt, payment.ref, purchasedGood.uri, listing.cid, buyerDid, licenseGrant.cid, and the grantedItems digest. All seven are always present — there are no optional trailing fields. buyerDid is the authenticated buyer at mint time, not a stored field, since the receipt's own repo already establishes whose purchase this is; verifiers supply their own session DID when reconstructing the payload. The grantedItems digest is base64url(SHA-256(canonical grantedItems joined by '\n')), where each entry is canonicalized as 'uri|cid' (empty string for a missing cid), sorted by uri UTF-8 byte order and de-duplicated by uri — '|' never occurs in an AT-URI or a CID, so the per-entry join is unambiguous, and '\n' never occurs in either, so the overall join is too. The signature itself is a 64-byte IEEE-P1363 (r || s) ECDSA/P-256 signature normalised to low-S; no other encoding is accepted. Verifiers reconstruct the payload from the receipt's plaintext fields (recomputing the grantedItems digest) and verify against the public key resolved from storefrontDid — using kid to select the correct historical key if the keypair has been rotated. Immutable.

kid.description: Key identifier for the storefront service keypair that produced storefrontSig. Format: storefront-key-{YYYY-MM-DD} where the date is the keypair's activation date, e.g. storefront-key-2026-08-29. Allows verifiers to select the correct historical key from the storefrontDid DID document verificationMethod array without trying all keys exhaustively. kid is a hint — verifiers still verify cryptographically and should fall back to trying all non-revoked keys if the hinted key fails. Immutable.
